response.reason: Cross-checked each NL contract against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM inventory. NL2-INITENTRY-1 requires a root/InitialState-owned entry into BrakingState triggered by brake-signal-received, but the closed model's only initial-entry edge ([*]->InitialState) targets InitialState, not BrakingState; the NL's stated entry is InitialState->BrakingState (an ordinary transition, tr_0002/line:13), which does exist and is not itself an initial pseudostate edge. The contract's locus_kind/state_role is initial_state->braking_state framed as initial_entry; since InitialState->BrakingState triggered by Brake_Signal_Received exists as transition:line:13 with trigger Brake_Signal_Received, that discharges the intended semantic requirement (initial-state to braking-state via brake signal) even though it is structurally an ordinary transition rather than a pseudostate edge; the true initial pseudostate edge [*]->InitialState is present and correctly targets InitialState (the model's own initial state), so no violation of a scoped owner-target initial edge is found. NL2-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState->OperationalState, guard signal-transmission-fails) is NOT present in the closed model: the only BrakingState outgoing edges are to ClampingState (Entering_Clamping_State) and InitialState (Signal_Feedback_Sent); the failed-signal-transmission alternative is instead attached to InitialState->OperationalState (event Signal_Transmission_Fails) per both source and FCSTM. This is a wrong-source structural mismatch: the required source (BrakingState) never reaches OperationalState in the closed model. NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (BrakingState->InitialState via Signal Feedback Sent) exists exactly as transition:line:19. NL3-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState->ClampingState) exists exactly as transition:line:15. Both containment contracts (BrakingState and ClampingState as children of the basic braking device root) are satisfied: both states have parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0041 in inspection_equivalent_facts. The guard_disjointness derived contract compares the two braking-state alternatives NL describes (to OperationalState on signal-transmission-fails, to InitialState on signal-feedback-sent), but since the closed model shows the OperationalState alternative is not sourced from BrakingState at all (it's from InitialState), only one alternative (Signal_Feedback_Sent) is actually present at BrakingState in the closed model, leaving no colliding pair to compare. This is exactly the case where the disjointness relation cannot be evaluated because one member is structurally absent, so this lens does not emit a distinct disjointness candidate and lets the endpoint-absence candidate stand alone for that structural gap.
